name: Material information a buyer should get before an offer

sources.title: National Trading Standards Estate and Letting Agency Team: Material information, quick guide for property agents (v1.0, November 2023), summary table of Parts A, B and C
MHCLG consultation: Material information in property listings (updated 19 June 2026), proposed list of categories

note: The National Trading Standards guide was published for estate agents. The government consulted from October to December 2025 on new guidance under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024; its proposed list covers the same items.

groups.title: Always needed
groups.description: Part A: costs and terms that matter for every home.

items.label: Council tax band
items.help: Sets your yearly council tax bill. Ask the agent.

items.label: Tenure, and any lease length, ground rent or service charge
items.help: Freehold or leasehold, and any costs you cannot avoid. Your conveyancer checks the title.

groups.title: Needed for every home
groups.description: Part B: facts the agent should find out for every home.

items.label: Property type and how it is built
items.help: For example terraced or detached; standard build, thatched roof or prefabricated.

items.label: Number and types of room
items.help: Bedrooms, bathrooms and living space, ideally with a floor plan.

items.label: Electricity, water, sewerage and heating
items.help: How each is supplied, for example mains water or a septic tank, gas or electric heating.

items.label: Broadband and mobile signal
items.help: What speeds and coverage are available at the address.

items.label: Parking
items.help: Whether there is a space, a garage, a permit zone or on-street parking only.

groups.title: Needed if it affects the home
groups.description: Part C: check whether each applies. Ask the agent and your conveyancer.

items.label: Building safety
items.help: For example cladding, fire safety or structural problems.

items.label: Restrictions
items.help: For example a listed building, a conservation area or limits on how the home can be used.

items.label: Rights and easements
items.help: For example a neighbour’s right of way, shared drives or wayleaves for cables and pipes.

items.label: Flood, coastal erosion and mining risk
items.help: Whether the home is at risk of flooding or erosion, or sits in a coalfield or mining area.

items.label: Planning permission and nearby developments
items.help: Approved or proposed building work at the home or close by.

items.label: Accessibility and adaptations
items.help: For example step-free access, a ramp or a stairlift.
